label: 3v
quote: Man rechne selbst mit den Widersprüchen! Was bedeutet dann dass die Theorie der Widersprüche widerspruchslos sein soll.
english: Let one calculate even with the contradictions! What then does it mean that the theory of contradictions should be consistent?
topic: Philosophical notes on the foundations of mathematics: Kant's question, contradictions, Lindelöf's rejection of aleph_1, mathematics and philosophy, the 'ignorabimus', who understood Helmholtz and Einstein, prophecy, and why simple special problems such as the four-colour problem are hard.

triage.modern_statement: The note is a philosophical remark, not a well-defined mathematical problem. Two modern readings fit the wording. (a) Hilbert's program reading: treat formulas and proofs as formal objects, contradictory ones included, and 'calculate' with them. Then the metatheory that studies these contradictions (proof theory) must itself be consistent, so what does that consistency requirement mean, and how could it be proved without circularity? (b) Paraconsistent reading: can a theory contain contradictions and still be non-trivial, i.e. not prove everything? If so, what does it mean to call the theory that handles those contradictions 'consistent'? The note's own wording does not settle which reading Hilbert meant.
triage.answered_by: There is no single answer. Under reading (a), Hilbert's own program of the 1920s took up the question by asking for finitary consistency proofs of formalized mathematics. Gödel's incompleteness theorems (1931) showed that such a system cannot prove its own consistency. Under reading (b), paraconsistent logic deals with inconsistent but non-trivial theories, starting with Jaśkowski (1948) and da Costa (1950s–1963).

evidence.claim: Gödel's incompleteness theorems (1931) showed that Hilbert's program could not be carried out for key areas of mathematics. By the second theorem, such a system cannot prove its own consistency.
Under Hilbert's Program, the consistency proof had to be carried out using only finitary methods. Historians still debate how Gödel's theorems affected the program.
Paraconsistent logic handles inconsistency in a controlled way, so a theory with contradictions need not become trivial.
Jaśkowski (1948) and, independently, da Costa (1963) proposed the two historically important approaches to paraconsistency.
Newton da Costa was one of the first pioneers of paraconsistent logic, in Brazil in the 1950s, and worked mainly on paraconsistent mathematics.

triage.why: The note is a one-line rhetorical question on a page of philosophical notes. It does not state a mathematical claim that could be checked. It is not one of the 23 problems or the 24th problem. Both readings tie into well-documented later work: consistency proofs and their limits after Gödel, and paraconsistent logic. Both fields are still actively researched, but neither can be shown to answer this specific note. I found no source that discusses this diary entry, so linking it to either line of work is my interpretation, not a documented connection.
